requirements.requirement: Record every sudo command run on node1 to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, including user and timestamp
requirements.summary: sudoers Defaults syslog=local2 was applied and validated (visudo -cf OK), and captured log tails show entries such as 'Sep 29 11:05:34 node1 sudo: antrieb : TTY=unknown ; PWD=... ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/echo sudo-log-test-...' both before and after the reboot, demonstrating user, timestamp, and command are captured for each sudo invocation.

requirements.requirement: Keep sudo-command log entries out of the general system log (syslog/auth.log)
requirements.summary: An rsyslog rule routes local2.* to the dedicated log file with a 'stop' directive preventing fallthrough to the default *.* rule that feeds /var/log/syslog. Marker commands run before and after reboot showed 0 matches in /var/log/syslog and /var/log/auth.log while appearing correctly in sudo-commands.log.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id f19de998-... with rsyslog active, sudoers file present, and log at 8 lines. Restart was acknowledged immediately via backgrounded 'shutdown -r now'. Node became briefly unreachable (connection refused) then returned with a new boot_id (9d3c443d-...), matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart checks confirmed rsyslog active, sudoers config persisted, and a fresh marker sudo command logged correctly to sudo-commands.log only, demonstrating full recovery of the configured logging behavior.

overall_summary: The executor correctly implemented sudo command logging on node1 via sudoers 'Defaults syslog=local2' plus a dedicated rsyslog rule with a stop directive, verified command entries (with user/timestamp) land only in /var/log/sudo-commands.log and are absent from syslog/auth.log both before and after a full reboot cycle with a directly observed boot-identity change. All material task outcomes and the independent restart-evidence protocol are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence, and no unnecessary or unreverted mutations were introduced.
limitations: Evidence relies on executor-selected command output excerpts rather than full raw log file contents, though the excerpts directly address each requirement.

Auth.log/session-open entries from PAM (distinct from sudo's own command-execution log line) were not separately examined, though this is outside the task's literal scope of 'commands run through sudo'.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (sudoers snippet creation, rsyslog conf creation, log file creation/permissions, rsyslog restart, and the deliberate reboot) map directly to satisfying the task or to producing the required restart evidence. Nonzero return codes observed (cmd-114789532e78453a, cmd-4622611bfce44c56, cmd-6efd5aec13ed4486) stem from expected behaviors — 'cat' denied on a 0440 sudoers file and 'grep -c' exiting 1 on zero matches — not real failures or unnecessary mutations. Lifecycle diffs show only the expected boot-identity change and reboot-generated systemd-private temp dirs; no residue, abandoned files, failed services, or unsafe exposure were introduced.
